main_topics.reason: The user opened asking which RA drugs are safe while trying and during pregnancy, and it drove most of the conversation.
The user disclosed being on methotrexate, asked if they should worry, and discussed contraception and washout.
The user asked for the ideal sequence for trying in 18 months and for what to do if the new drugs control RA less well.
The user asked whether pregnancy-safe meds are also okay with breastfeeding, for one exchange.
The user asked whether RA changes in pregnancy and learned about postpartum flares.
The user asked who to coordinate with and whether to raise pregnancy plans with their rheumatologist now.
The user said they were scared of choosing between health and a baby and left feeling less anxious.
The user asked what happens if the new medication controls RA less well, a single exchange.

output.summary: A user two months into an RA diagnosis, planning a pregnancy in 1-2 years, asked which RA medications are safe around conception and pregnancy. They learned they are on methotrexate and need to stop it at least 3 months before trying, got a timeline, and heard about postpartum flares and breastfeeding. They planned to raise it with their rheumatologist and said they left feeling less anxious and with a handle on it.
